summary: postinstall mutates installer's package.json to inject an unpinned third-party dependency
details: randompkga@1.0.14 ships no library code (no README, no index.js, no runtime source). Its sole payload is a postinstall lifecycle script that reads the consumer project's package.json at process.env.INIT_CWD, adds a new dependency entry 'randompkgb': '^1.0.0', and rewrites the manifest on disk. On the next install (and in any downstream consumer that installs the modified project), npm will resolve and execute code from randompkgb — an unpinned, floating third-party package controlled by a separate publisher — expanding the installer's dependency graph with code the installer never chose. This is dependency-tree hijacking via manifest mutation: the mechanism runs automatically on `npm install` and grants the author of randompkgb code execution inside the installer's project on subsequent installs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
